name: Question 3
worked_solution:
We break up the integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }\frac{4{x}^{3}}{{(2+{x}^{4})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x={\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{4{x}^{3}}{{(2+{x}^{4})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{4{x}^{3}}{{(2+{x}^{4})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x
$$

First, we calculate the antiderivative using a substitution. Let $u=2+{x}^{4}$,  then $\text{d}u=4{x}^{3}\text{d}x.$ Hence

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4{x}^{3}}{{(2+{x}^{4})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{u}+C \\  & =-\frac{1}{2+{x}^{4}}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

We now evaluate the first of the improper integrals, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{4{x}^{3}}{{(2+{x}^{4})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{0}\frac{4{x}^{3}}{{(2+{x}^{4})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }({-\frac{1}{2+{x}^{4}}|}_{a}^{0}) \\  & =-{lim}_{a\to -\infty }(\frac{1}{2+0}-\frac{1}{2+{a}^{4}}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}+0 \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the integrand is an **odd** function. This means that we can immediately deduce that 

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{4{x}^{3}}{{(2+{x}^{4})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Therefore, since both improper integrals exist, we conclude that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }\frac{4{x}^{3}}{{(2+{x}^{4})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{4{x}^{3}}{{(2+{x}^{4})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{4{x}^{3}}{{(2+{x}^{4})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

We break up the integral as follows:

∫−∞∞4x3(2+x4)2dx=∫−∞04x3(2+x4)2dx+∫0∞4x3(2+x4)2dx

First, we calculate the antiderivative using a substitution. Let u=2+x4, then du=4x3dx. Hence ∫4x3(2+x4)2dx=∫1u2du=−1u+C=−12+x4+C. We now evaluate the first of the improper integrals, as follows:

∫−∞04x3(2+x4)2dx=lima→−∞∫a04x3(2+x4)2dx=lima→−∞(−12+x4|a0)=−lima→−∞(12+0−12+a4)=−12+0=−12.

Now, notice that the integrand is an odd function. This means that we can immediately deduce that

∫0∞4x3(2+x4)2dx=12.

Therefore, since both improper integrals exist, we conclude that ∫−∞∞4x3(2+x4)2dx=∫−∞04x3(2+x4)2dx+∫0∞4x3(2+x4)2dx=−12+12=0.
